title: Taking groups out and playing Cleveland with Red Richards and Eddie Condon
summary: He took no groups of his own to Toronto or Chicago, but played Cleveland dozens of times with Red Richards's Saints and Sinners and with Eddie Condon.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did the groups that you took into the Embers play with you anyplace else? Or was it just a one-shot thing with whoever you took in?

Well, possibly sometimes you would run -- you would have -- you'd get tied into something else, but just in for the Embers, or should, you have a few other dates, a couple of other dates, to hang on there, you told the guys well, when we finish here we're going into such and such a place. Can you, or will you, go in there with me? One of those things, you know?
Did you play Toronto with those kind of groups.
With the group? No, No, I didn't take a group into Toronto, of my own. I did not.
Or the London House in Chicago, or the Theatrical Grille in Cleveland?
No, I played -- no, I didn't take any
groups into Cleveland, but I went in there with Red, oh my God, dozens of times, I guess.
Now Red, you're talking about Red Richards now.
Yeah, right. So Saints and Sinners, and who else did I go with? Oh, I went in there -- at Cleveland, I went in there with Eddie --
No, no. Cabaret owner Cat --- Eddie Condon.

Well I worked with Eddie Condon, oh, many times, and here and there, but we played Cleveland, and who else did I go in there with? Besides Eddie, I'm trying to think. Eddie and -- and -- the Saints -- Red Richards. I think that was all there, in that particular place. Uh-huh.
